title: 14.2 A 16nm 216kb, 188.4TOPS/W and 133.5TFLOPS/W Microscaling Multi-Mode Gain-Cell CIM Macro Edge-AI Devices
problem: CIM macros face tradeoffs: integer CIM achieves high energy efficiency but limited accuracy; floating-point CIM provides higher accuracy but reduced efficiency; emerging microscaling (MX) formats improve accuracy-efficiency but require novel multi-mode CIM supporting MX-INT-FP with: system-to-CIM transfer overhead, costly adder trees, and inefficient data flows across variable accumulation sizes.
motivation: Optimal AI data format is workload-dependent; edge AI requires flexible CIM supporting multiple precision modes without excessive energy/area overhead.
method: 16nm 216kb gain-cell CIM supporting MX-INT-FP modes via: multi-mode input processing unit (M2-IPU) with SS-variance-aware MAC flow handling FP2MX inside CIM, pattern-aware hybrid adder tree (PAH-ADT) reducing high-probability ops, accumulation-aware data flow (A2-DF) dynamically reconfiguring write paths.
key_novelty: Multi-mode input processing with in-CIM format conversion and pattern-aware adder tree optimizing flexibility across MX/INT/FP formats.
contributions: In-CIM format conversion eliminating system-to-CIM overhead
primary_theme: Multi-mode CIM macro supporting flexible precision formats for edge AI
